solution:
Factorise each term as a difference of squares. First: \(\frac{(p - q + r)(p + q - r)}{(p + r - q)(p + r + q)} = \frac{p + q - r}{p + q + r}\).

Second: \(\frac{(q - p + r)(q + p - r)}{(p + q - r)(p + q + r)} = \frac{q + r - p}{p + q + r}\). Third: \(\frac{(r - p + q)(r + p - q)}{(q + r - p)(q + r + p)} = \frac{r + p - q}{p + q + r}\).

Sum of numerators \(= p + q + r\), so the value is \(1\).

Check: \(p = 4, q = 2, r = 1\) gives \(\frac{15}{21} - \frac{5}{35} + \frac{3}{7} = \frac{5}{7} - \frac{1}{7} + \frac{3}{7} = 1\).
note: p = 3, q = 2, r = 1 makes the third denominator 0
